newsitem.title: URUGUAY: Divers raise Graf Spee gun from River Plate.
newsitem.headline: Divers raise Graf Spee gun from River Plate.

text.p: Uruguayan and British divers have recovered one of the guns of the German World War Two "pocket battleship" Admiral Graf Spee from the muddy waters of the River Plate, they said on Wednesday.

"The cannon is safe," Uruguayan diver Hector Bado told Reuters from the dive site off Montevideo, where divers and scientists from Britain's Oxford University, the Uruguayan Navy and cable television Discovery Channel had refloated a cannon nine yards (eight metres) long and weighing 50 tons.
In the 1939 Battle of the River Plate, the pride of the German fleet, the Graf Spee, was hunted down to the South Atlantic by the British warships Exeter, Ajax and Achilles.

Small but lethally effective, the German ship was hit and cornered in December 1939 and found shelter for four days in Montevideo. But diplomatic pressure forced it into the open sea and Capt. Hans Langsdorff sank it rather than surrender his command.
Three days later he killed himself with a gun in the nearby Argentine capital Buenos Aires.
Discovery Channel has filmed the dive, which took place 11 yards (10 metres) deep in the brown waters of the River Plate. The cannon was raised by an 80-ton crane mounted on tugs.
"Underneath the water visibility was very poor, practically zero, so we had to work by touch," said Bado.

The find should be of interest to military historians since the Graf Spee, built in 1934, was armed with the latest secret military technology of the day, including a decoder known as "Enigma" which would have made it a valuable prize.

"You will understand, my decision was not easy," the doomed Langsdorff wrote to his wife before sinking his ship.. "The English had us surrounded so that it was impossible for us to get out of the port of Montevideo fighting."
British Admiral Lord Mountbatten described the Battle of the River Plate as "the last naval battle without aircraft carriers, submarines, destroyers or efficient radars."
But Bado and his fellow divers are not interested in more dives on the pocket battleship: "For us the Graf Spee is over, we've seen it and we don't plan to do anything else."
